objective: maximize note revenue by combining free acquisition/demand-validation articles with paid conversion articles while preserving the existing paid publication floor

internalEvidence.interpretation: There is not yet enough first-party evidence to claim that paid-only publishing is optimal or to identify a proven winning theme. Therefore use a measured acquisition/conversion funnel and update the mix when first-party results appear.

findings: note editorial guidance recommends using reactions to free articles and social posts as signals for paid-content demand.
note editorial guidance recommends cross-linking related free and paid articles to increase circulation and purchase opportunities.

note editorial analysis of 100 frequently purchased Business/IT paid articles found three common free-area elements: empathy/question framing, a change or before/after story, and a clear statement of reader benefit.
note guidance recommends making the free portion useful on its own rather than placing nearly all value behind the paywall.

2026 note changes include improved discovery/category surfaces, AI-readable creator pages via llms.txt, and easier membership onboarding; these increase the value of building a reusable free-content surface rather than relying only on isolated paid posts.

paid.rule: Do not reduce or replace this floor with free articles. Reader-visible URL, exact title, expected price, paid boundary and dedicated cover are still required before a paid publication counts.

initialExperiment.note: 2/day is an experimental starting cadence, not a proven optimum. Manuscripts may be produced in larger batches and scheduled gradually to avoid quality dilution or feed flooding.

contentRules: Every free article must provide standalone practical value.
Do not publish thin teaser-only posts.
Use at most one context-matched paid CTA per free article.
Only insert a paid URL after that URL has been independently reader-visible verified; never guess URLs.

Prefer problem diagnosis, checklists, mistakes, quick wins, frameworks and small worked examples for free articles; reserve deeper implementation systems, templates, full workflows and reusable assets for paid articles.

batchProduction.rule: Article creation itself is mandatory work, not optional analysis. Production may be batched. A production run may create multiple complete manuscripts at once rather than one manuscript per run.
batchProduction.preferredBatchSize: 4-10 complete manuscripts when quality can be maintained
batchProduction.minimumArtifactRule: A note-focused production run must end with at least one newly completed article manuscript; strategy analysis, backlog edits or retry instructions alone do not count as article creation.
batchProduction.backlogRule: Maintain multiple ready free and paid manuscripts so one stuck article never blocks the pipeline.

funnelArchitecture.ctaRule: One related CTA after the useful free core. No unrelated multi-product CTA stack.
funnelArchitecture.reverseLinkRule: Paid articles should also link to useful free companion articles when doing so helps readers understand context or discover the series.

rules: Do not compare raw lifetime PV between articles of different ages; use comparable post-publication windows.
Free articles with above-median engagement or meaningful paid-outbound evidence become candidates for paid deep dives.
Paid articles with observed sales should receive supporting free satellite articles around adjacent search intent.
If a free theme attracts traffic but produces no paid movement after sufficient exposure, test CTA/value proposition before producing more paid derivatives.
If neither traffic nor engagement appears, deprioritize that theme rather than mass-cloning it.
